name: Seneca Chamber arbitrary-call approval drain
summary: Chamber's public performOperations exposed an OPERATION_CALL action with attacker-controlled target and calldata. Because users had standing token allowances to their Chamber, an attacker could make the Chamber call token.transferFrom(victim, attacker, balance) and drain approved wallet assets.

loss.notes: The reported $6.4 million gross campaign loss covers repeated approval drains from Seneca users on Ethereum and Arbitrum. Approximately $5.3 million was later returned under a 20% bounty; recovery is separate from exploit-time gross loss.

lastCodeChange.description: The EIP-1167 clone hard-coded the defect-bearing Chamber implementation at deployment and cannot be repointed.

limitations: Aged from the clone rather than the shared implementation it copies; not yet re-examined under the clone rule in METHODOLOGY.md.

sources.note: Reviewed the successful Ethereum exploit receipt and call trace, clone creation trace, exact EIP-1167 runtime, implementation deployment and historical runtime, commit-pinned reproduction, and technical campaign-loss reporting. Attacker 0x94641c01a4937f2c8ef930580cf396142a2942dc directly calls performOperations on Chamber clone 0x65c210c59b43eb68112b7a4f75c8393c36491f06, which delegates to 0x45e15d1e4f92f28a916f4f2971ad9adc278e148b and makes the attacker-specified token transferFrom call using the clone's standing allowance. Factory 0xf5bce5077908a1b7370b9ae04adc565ebd643966 CREATE2-deployed the clone in block 19264402; its 45-byte runtime hard-codes the implementation, hashes to 0xed29dfd9225e2baa5c1af63bac1c516433cf3d8c0f93cf2abc7660a70f4069f4, and cannot be repointed. The implementation was directly deployed in block 19215501 by protocol deployer 0x61da869d8eb130cb3d2ba5bbd57c4a53ff534cb4. Its 22,816-byte runtime hashes to 0x4bcc3eb4a0d18e14d3658e127d3afd7796dac06af7f875272a7af9767f22c39e at clone creation and immediately before the exploit and contains no further DELEGATECALL. The reported campaign drained $6.4 million across Seneca markets on Ethereum and Arbitrum; about $5.3 million was later returned.

limitations: The $6.4 million gross loss is a rounded reported cross-chain campaign total rather than a per-transfer incident-time valuation; later recovery is recorded separately.
